name: Benaiah
overview: Benaiah is a male figure identified as a descendant of Pahath-moab who had married a foreign wife, as noted in Ezra 10:30. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal notes recorded about him. His mention is brief and specific to his lineage and marital connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Benaiah means 'y-h-v-h has built,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's role in establishment or construction. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine involvement.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Benaiah as a descendant of Pahath-moab. Beyond this relationship and his association with a foreign wife, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Benaiah's significance lies in his representation of the post-exilic community's challenges, particularly concerning intermarriage with foreign wives as addressed in Ezra 10:30. His identity underscores the complexities of maintaining covenantal purity and faithfulness to God during the restoration period. This highlights the broader biblical theme of obedience to God's commands in the context of Israel's return from exile.
